title: Blood: One Unit Whole Blood
text: Blood is a 90s old school shooter and is also the most underrated and under looked shooter of all time. The story is that you play as Caleb who is a gunslinger who’s friends are killed and he is buried alive and he wants revenge… that’s it… that’s the story… if you were expecting more you are playing this the wrong way since this is an old school shooter and the story matters the least and is forgotten during gameplay. The theme of the game is horror, the kind of satanic and supposedly dark and disturbing horror but this game isn’t meant to be taken seriously at all. The gameplay is basically the same as Duke Nukem 3d but much better, nearly everything that was in Duke 3d is in blood and used better and made to fit the theme and doesn’t suffer from any of the problems found in Duke 3d, those being: blowing yourself up too much with the rocket launcher and the tedious level design and key hunts that will have you aimlessly wondering around a level when you’ve killed everyone. Blood is also the most violent game of the 90s, and it’s really fun to group up some enemies and blow them to pieces or blow their skin off by using the napalm rocket launcher or a bundle of dynamite and have Caleb laughing like a sadistic madman. The weapons you get consists of a pitchfork, a flair gun, a sawn off shotgun, a tommy gun, a napalm rocket launcher, three different variations of dynamite, spray cans, a telsa gun, a voodoo doll and a staff. The majority of these weapons have alternate fire, with the flair gun you can either fire one flair or fire a huge fire ball, with the shotgun you can either fire one barrel at a time or both at once, with the tommy gun you can either just plain fire it or you can fire it so it sways to the left and right which is good for a wide group of enemies, with the napalm launcher you can either fire it like a rocket launcher or a grenade launcher, with the spray cans you can either use it as a flamethrower or you can fire bomb enemies with it. Why this game is underrated and under looked: At the time of its release people would rather play quake 2 because it has a fully 3d engine when blood is 2.5D and the game almost became forgotten which is quite pathetic because this is a massively better game than quake 2. There aren’t really any problems with the game itself but there are a few very small irritations with the difficulty and that being that all of the enemies with guns are pixel pin point accurate and do not miss a single shot and have really quick reactions where sometimes you’ll open a door and you get killed immediately, and with enemies that use projectiles they tent to fire to the left and right hitting you every single time since your natural reaction is to strafe left and right. If you like old school shooters definitely get this game without a doubt it’s always fun to play.

title: Blood: One Unit Whole Blood
text: NOTE: I had issues running this well on steam. I was forced to utilize outside means and customazation options to get blood to work properly. Using bloodGDX was a great help and was useful in many ways including getting the expansion pack to work with minimal issues. My review may be affected by this as I don't know how many changes happened as a result and could have effected my experince from the vanilla blood game. This guide from a user named colek can help get bloodGDX if you desire. Blood is a FPS that uses the build engine like duke nukem 3D and shadow warrior. The graphics are really solid with attention to detail(for the time), and if you like gore this won't hold back. You will see organs fly and blood everywhere, so be aware it's not for the squemish. With some grewsome enviorments like decomposing corpses and a dark tone, this has a very thick atmosphere of dread that holds up 20 years later. The sound design is very effective, giving you chills as you hear enemies scream in agony and hear splats of violence. The sound track ties all this together with a very oninomus tone. The controls are just like the other build games and work well, but you may want to configure the controls a bit, as the layout can feel a little chaotic by default. Also swimming is a real pain as you have to tap c repeatedly to swim down, you can jump in water to dive quicker but it doesn't change the fact it feels a bit awkward, on the plus side water sections don't last too long. The gameplay is very satisfiying with a wide range of weapons like dynamite and a tommygun but can also get a bit unorthodox like a voodoo doll(my fav) or tesla gun. Most of these weapons also have alt fire modes, varying up how you can approch enemies. And rounding it all out is defensive items like medkits and boots to help you jump higher and a few others. There's also plenty of replay value with many secrets, references to horror films, and hidden levels. The expansion pack was every bit as good as the main game. It wasn't just more levels, this added new ideas for level layouts and while you don't get new weapons or fight new enemies, it had some of the best levels due to cool puzzle ideas and new ways they used them. If it was an episode on the main game it would probably be my favorite despite how much I enjoyed the others. While this won't effect my review I should point out that the modding community is alive and well with some talented users that make great content. So if you enjoy using mods then this one has that in spades. Overall with it's creepy atmosphere, satisfying gameplay, great replay value, and large amount of content(even without mods) this was one of the best FPS's i've played on steam.

text: $5 by default, around $1.25 during a sale, this is a huge bargain and probably the best Steam game you can get for $5 or less. Blood, along with Duke Nukem 3D and Shadow Warrior are among the best games to use the Build engine, but I think Blood is the greatest of all three of them. If you are big horror movie fan or a fan of the Evil Dead movies, then you will love this game. I would recommend it to anyone who is a big fan of classic first person shooters and horror films. This is my second favorite fps game of all time behind only the original Doom because in all fairness, Blood wouldn't exist without the success of Doom. I will go as far and say this game is a masterpiece and it really defined what 90's first person shooters were all about. Buy this game, you will not be disappointed, 10 out of 10.

title: Blood: One Unit Whole Blood
text: There are 3 different Build Engine games that really count: Duke Nukem, Blood, Shadow Warrior. They all basically play the same in that you are a smartass with lots of interesting and bizarre weapons going level to level, massacring everything in your path and collecting keys to progress. Blood is the horror one of these three for sure. The game's plot is basically cult member who got screwed over by a demon is reborn and♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off. The protagonist is just as clever and enjoyable as Lo Wang or Duke and personally my favourite of the three. The weapons are quite fun and you really do feel like a sadist when you light up people with a flare gun and they scream like mad. It fits the protagonist's character extremely well. The level design is not as frustrating in regards to key hunting. I never needed a FAQ or to even look at the map though some secrets are really hard to find. The game is quite long I feel and there are 5 difficulty levels so you don't ever rage quit because of it being too difficult. It is packed with horror references from films and books even in the tiniest places. The protagonist is also quite witty and the voice acting is really cool. For younger gamers some of these will go over their heads since they didn't grow up reading Lovecraft or watching Phantasm for example. But as a 28 year old gamer I am constantly chuckling at the various references. Also, it has numerous mods available. All in all I think if you enjoy the Build Engine games then you will enjoy Blood but it is a great plus if you are an older horror fan.

title: Bloodbath Kavkaz
text: It's a shameless knock-off of Hotline Miami, and they're not even hiding it (It even had "Hotline" in the title until they were forced to change it because of the copyright.) The basics are pretty much the same, only the controls are flimsy and awkward, the AI is ridiculous, and the camera being too zoomed-in combined with bad level design makes this game barely playable (It likes to call itself hardcore, but there's nothing challenging about constantly being shot down by enemies you can't even possibly see in front of you, it's just crap.) Also it's rather buggy, just to name a few, I had to often restart the levels because I kept clipping through walls with no way to get back, and it randomly switches and locks the language to Russian forcing me to reboot the game. How it fares graphically everyone can see. It's poorly drawn and layered with bunch of filters to clumsily copy the Hotline Miami's stylistic choices (but it's not very well done. At some points the layering was so heavy that I actually got a headache from it.) The music is a bit more interesting topic, but not for the right reasons. It was stolen at first, but when the composer found out about it and requested that they remove his music from the game, the developers started to constantly pester and bully him until he gave up just to get away from them. So officially they have the rights to use his music in the game, and it doesn't have much to do with the game itself and its quality (in my opinion it doesn't compare to the Hotline Miami, but to each his own, I'm sure some people like it,) but at the very least it shows what kind of disgusting people the developers are. I have no idea why anyone would choose this game over Hotline Miami, especially since the price difference is only €1, but if you got it somehow, the rickroll that plays at the first startup of the game should tell you how much you just got screwed over.

title: Bloodbath Kavkaz
text: Now I know what you're thinking: is just a shameless ripoff of . Oh, if only.  No, is a "hilarious" "parody" of .  Or, put it another way, this is what would look like if nobody involved with its development were over the age of fifteen, save for one unfortunate musician who was relentlessly badgered into providing the admittedly great soundtrack. Naturally the game can't ape anything properly from its influence.  Whereas HM based its challenge around planning and tactics, BK instead opts for horrid controls and limited visibility.  Movement is incredibly awkward.  The player character lurches ahead too quickly for any kind of precision and often gets stuck on walls and furniture.  There's also no lock-on feature, so don't even bother fighting while moving.  Meanwhile, your visual range is very narrow, so most kills are made by firing blindly down the hall, and the eye-searing visual effects make it harder still to aim. Fortunately, you do have two advantages: First, the AI is very dumb.  Once alerted, it will just bounce off the walls until it can line up a shot, which is highly exploitable if you're careful.  Second, it's very easy to glitch yourself in and out of the level, so if you don't have to kill anything in a stage you can just bypass the enemies and head straight to the goal. Ultimately my breaking point was a vehicle section in which you must avoid two instant kills, one of which is positioned randomly.  Once I realized just how little control I had over the outcome, I gave it a few more hopeful tries and finally ragequit. That's not even getting into the script, which is a cringeworthy mess of bad jokes, nonsensical profanity, and outdated internet memes.  It might amuse those who lied to get around this page's age gate, but adult players will most likely find it incredibly grating.  The only laughs I got out of it were when the abysmal English translation mangled a line beyond comprehension. ♥♥♥♥ this game, ♥♥♥♥ the unfunny hacks who made it, ♥♥♥♥ Steam and IndieGala for allowing it on their services, and most of all, ♥♥♥♥ ME for actually attempting to play it!  This is my worst game of 2015 so far, and I pray to the gaming gods that nothing comes around to top it.

title: Bloodbath Kavkaz
text: Good game with a lot of glitches.  If you liked Hotline Miami 1 & 2 and you want more of that, definitely get this game.  However, I can pretty much 100% guarantee you that you will encounter glitches in which you walk through outer walls.  The good news is, the glitches aren't game-breaking and you can usually exploit them by just walking to an exit or staircase to reach the next or previous area. I believe I only encountered 2 times in which I had to reset the level because nothing I was pressing was working - one was at a computer that has several things to click on it and wouldn't let me exit and the other was during a sexual intercourse simulation scene.  However, the stages are so short that having to reset a stage is not a big deal.  Most stages don't require everyone to be defeated, so you can go straight to the mission objective and exit a stage with having only killed a few people. After beating the game once, I was able to breeze through the other difficulty settings (for achievements) and beat the game in about 2.5 hours on each run.  It took me just under 14 hours to 100% the game.  The AI isn't extremely smart, but the enemies can usually detect when bullets are being shot by you and will come to your direction.  Unlike the Hotline Miami games, you will not have bullets being shot at you from across the screen that you can not see.  I believe the enemies only shoot at you when you are close to their view. The game has good music, however, the stages are so short that no songs really got stuck in my head.  That's not exactly a bad thing though.  Also, I should point out that there are a few areas in the game in which I would advise of a "seizure warning" due to the constantly flashing lights.

text: Imagine a combination of Hotline Miami and the worst game ever. Bloodbath Kavkaz is just so hella trashy that it's actually fun. There's a lame sexual intercourse minigame with button mashing from hell, which is at least optional and unlocks an achievement. Now let's take a look at the good things: It has some neat features like a hat (similar to the masks in HM) which enables slow motion. Enemies actually talk, or at least shout stuff when they see you or die. The voice acting is so unbelievably bad, it makes you laugh all the time. Gives the game an interesting touch. It has exploding barrels. It actually has some really entertaining levels, such as ♥♥♥♥ing a building with exploding barrels and uncountable enemies up with a minigun. For some reason there's a pineapple speaking arabic. In the background there's a kind of techno song with some guy shouting "ANANAS". I will never forget this scene in my life. Neutral: Even if you switch the game to English, some lines haven't been translated. For some reason, the main menu is English when starting the game and  Russian when leaving it which is always quite fun. The DLC hasn't even translated to English. I see this as neutral because I'm currently learning Russian and therefore this is quite fun for me. Long story short: If you want to experience the best trash of you life, get this game for only a dollar on the next sale.

text: Flock of Rakk flew into my stationary vehicle's tires and exploded 10/10. On a more serious note, I haven't beaten the entire game, DLC and all, but I killed the , and I think that that's close enough to write a  complete review. I'm going to name a bunch of small things, then summarize my overall thoughts. The early-game SG43 Fatal Death Shotgun is amazing (accuracy 74.6), and I used it throughout the entire game, where it continued to be incredibly useful. This game would be hard if not for Second Winds. A lot of bosses have a lot of little guys helping them, and that's their downfall. Patricia Tannis' story is intriguing, and I wanted to see all of it. I respect Bandit Raiders. There, I said it. They joined a mercenary organization, and what do they do? They bring a big, menacing, puffy coat, a shield, and a GUN. And they take lots of cover and fire only from the shoulder. Overall, the combat can sometimes be annoying, especially near the end, but the story is good and the RPG mechanics work well. And the style and attitude are unmatched. Get it. title: Borderlands 2
text: Take a FPS add a dungeon crawler, take most of them away and add an open map. Take the ratchet and clank gun technology, with ES:IV drops, And halo co-op. Add great voice acting, and guess what you get? BORDERLANDS 2. If you liked halo you'll feel right at home with it and you'll easily adapt to the different playstyle. If you like offline dungeon crawlers you'll know that most of your equipment will be useless in a few levels and what to sell at the slightest glance. Quests are fun, co-op is perfect, and you will enjoy it to any extent no matter what. Playing alone is like elder scrolls, as in you'll advance just once and you'll get the drops and quest rewards one time unless there are special circumstances. But on co-op, you can relive absolutely every story and event your host has. want to see Lilith beg for eridium twice for no reason? grab a new player. The level system is akin to an mmo, but more forgiving. so for example, running into lower levelled enemies will give you a god mode feeling, as they'll be useless and dr5op nonsense that all you'll want to do is sell. Which is good, because you wont fly through the challenges simply by grinding through it. Though if the quest system matches it, you may want to do everything you want before hunting quests with rare rewards. As that was a very annoying case in Oblivion. Grab a few friends and try it out, it's pretty fun and interesting, And in my opinion it will last you a long time for entertainment. Though you may want to find a few fiends who understand how dungeon crawlers work, so they dont get stuck on equipment that obviously needs to be sold or dropped, purple or not. And the game has that message as a load screen. Levelling, is very exponential in my opinion, so like some of the broken rpg games out there, if you're struggling on something, better try to level up or buy a good shield before anything else, because shields and normal health have their pros and cons. After you understand the system, It'll be even mor fun to play and teach others how the system works, and you'll all e3njoy abusing the enemies in unison. Which is pretty perfect seeing as halo was insanely easy when you had a focused team. It's a pretty unique experience. So if you really want to try a fun shooter with friends, you should give it a go.

title: Borderlands 2
text: As someone with moderate experience in FPS games who never played a title in this franchise before, I can say that BL2 is a surprisingly good game. Possibly one of the best singleplayer FPS experiences I had in the past years. The game is a little dated with just over 4 years at the time of this writing. The underwhelming cel shading graphics look pretty trashy, but at least it runs well on high settings even on an older machine. It's the year 2900 and you are a treasure hunter on a lawless Prison Planet full of mad criminals, violent aliens and murderous robots. Nice soundtrack, pleasant gunplay, decently intelligent AI, optional 4 player coop and addictive gameplay with a potential up ro 100+ hours and more. To be entirely honest, I often felt as If I was playing a MMO with quite a lot of depth. Sadly, the Missions and level design gets somewhat same-ish, there is little to no difference in the gameplay of the (up to) 6 player classes, the overall product is riddled with paid DLC and the story is a load of pretentious bullshît garnered with bland, unlikeable bystanders. The exception being the antihero you fight, who is in itself quite excellent. On the other hand the female lead character is singlehandedly one of the most disgusting putrid cûnts I have seen in any piece of media to this day. Anthony Burch, the head writer for the storyline, is a fûcking marxist SJW cuck. I bought the GOTY Edition and not even there was all DLC inclusive. What the fûck Gearbox? I even bought Duke Nukem Forever at full price back in the day from you. Such greedy marketing is not necessary. The followup spinoff to BL2 from 2014 is not bad. They tweaked some parts of the formula. If you are not picky, you could like it. It's not as well done as the original or as long, but a nice experience nonetheless. It's a shame the responsible guest studio has been shut down in 2015. If you don't already own BL2, I can recommend this without a second thought if you like Scifi, Guns, or Loot based RPGs. It's more or less a one of a kind and dirt cheap during sales for less than 10 Euros. If you can warm up to an odd looking old goldie, go for it. What bang you get for the buck in the GOTY edition is borderline theft to your advantage. Here's hoping Gearbox can recover from the Battleborn trainwreck that Blizzard largely forced upon them last year. Hopefully BL3 will do well enough.

title: Borderlands 2
text: Pros: Story, Graphics, Sound, Controls, Gameplay Cons: Clothes Customization As one of four (six with DLC) vault hunters, you must stop the evil Handsome Jack from opening the vault.  Although Borderlands 2 recycles the basic plot of the first game, the twists, characters, and dialogue are extraordinary.  From the reflections of the environment in gun scopes to the smoldering volcanic ash falling from the sky, the graphics are superb.  From Miss Moxxi's sultry voice to the delicious splat of a midget psycho's head, the quality of the voice acting and sounds is perfect.  Controls are amazing: a joy to play with both a keyboard/mouse or a controller.  Millions upon millions of guns, a variety of different enemies, six unique classes, and up to three friends make one of the best games ever. No game is without its flaws however.  Character customization is limited to only head and body selection.  Well, perhaps no game is without its flaw. Borderlands 2 is simply awesome. 10/10
